verified: https://myaccount.google.com/security-checkup (official; g.co/securitycheckup redirects to the same page; signed-out visitors see /intro/security-checkup)

Google Account → Security → "How you sign in to Google" → 2-Step Verification (https://myaccount.google.com/signinoptions/twosv) and Passkeys and security keys. On iPhone: Gmail app → profile picture → Manage your Google Account → Security.
Google Account → Security → "How you sign in to Google" → Recovery phone / Recovery email
Google Account → Security → Your devices → Manage all devices (https://myaccount.google.com/device-activity)
Google Account → Security → Your connections to third-party apps & services (https://myaccount.google.com/connections)

Security alerts are always on and cannot be turned off; review them at Google Account → Security → Recent security activity (https://myaccount.google.com/notifications). Copy should say "check" not "turn on".
All 7 apply (alerts step = review, not toggle).

spec: Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security (no URL; covered by Apple steps)
verified: Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security (iOS 26). Apple has no web security checkup; web equivalent is https://account.apple.com → Sign-In and Security. Safety Check is separate (Settings → Privacy & Security → Safety Check).
Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication (on by default for nearly all accounts). Optional: Security Keys in the same screen.

Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication → trusted phone numbers (add a second number not tied to this iPhone); Account Recovery / Recovery Contact in the same Sign-In & Security screen.
Settings → [your name] → scroll to the device list → tap an unknown device → Remove from Account.

Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Sign in with Apple (apps using your Apple Account); app-specific passwords are managed at account.apple.com → Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords.
No toggle: Apple always sends sign-in approval prompts to trusted devices and email notices. Skip alerts step (or make it informational).
Apply: 2fa, unique_pw, recovery_info, sessions, third_party. Skip: alerts (automatic), checkup (no Apple checkup page; point to Safety Check instead).
https://account.microsoft.com/security (official Microsoft account Security dashboard; redirects to sign-in). Microsoft does not call it a 'checkup'; copy should say "Microsoft's security page".

account.microsoft.com/security → Manage how I sign in → Additional security → Two-step verification → Turn on. Passkeys are added from the same 'Manage how I sign in' page (Microsoft accounts are now passkey-first for new accounts).
account.microsoft.com/security → Manage how I sign in → 'Ways to prove who you are' (phone/email). Also generate a recovery code here.
Review: Security dashboard → Sign-in activity (https://account.live.com/activity). Sign out: Manage how I sign in → 'Sign out everywhere' (takes up to 24 h; not per-device).
'Apps and services that can access your data' at https://account.live.com/consent/Manage (linked from the Privacy/Security dashboards).
No user toggle; Microsoft automatically emails/texts on unusual sign-in. Make alerts step informational or skip.
Apply: 2fa, unique_pw, recovery_info, sessions (sign out everywhere), third_party, checkup. Skip/informational: alerts.
https://login.yahoo.com/myaccount/security (the spec URL still works but redirects here; hard-code the canonical one). Yahoo has no 'checkup' wizard; this is the Account Security page.

Account Security → 'Ways of signing in' → 2-Step Verification (phone, authenticator app, security key); Passkeys section on the same page. In Yahoo Mail iOS app: profile → Manage accounts → Account info → Security settings.
https://login.yahoo.com/myaccount/personalinfo → recovery phone and email (Account Info).
https://login.yahoo.com/myaccount/recentactivity (Recent activity → sign out of sessions you don't recognize).
Account Security → app passwords (delete unknown) and https://login.yahoo.com/myaccount/permissions (connected apps).
No toggle; Yahoo automatically notifies on security changes. Informational only.
Apply: 2fa, unique_pw, recovery_info, sessions, third_party, checkup (security page). Skip: alerts.
https://login.aol.com/myaccount/security (spec URL redirects here; use canonical).
Account Security page → 2-Step Verification (phone, authenticator app, security key).
Account Info → recovery phone/email (https://login.aol.com/myaccount/personalinfo).
https://login.aol.com/myaccount/recentactivity (Recent activity).
Account Security → app passwords; remove ones you don't use.
No toggle; AOL automatically emails primary and backup addresses on security changes. Informational.
Same as Yahoo: skip alerts toggle.

Facebook Help links Security Checkup at https://www.facebook.com/privacy/review?review_id=573933453011661 (could not confirm with an unauthenticated fetch).
Accounts Center → Password and security → Two-factor authentication (also Passkey, rolled out 2025).
Accounts Center → Personal details → Contact info.
Accounts Center → Password and security → Where you're logged in → Select devices to log out. (Some accounts show 'Meta Account settings' instead of Accounts Center.)
Settings & privacy → Settings → Apps and websites (under 'Your activity'/'Permissions').
Accounts Center → Password and security → Login alerts.

Profile → ☰ → Accounts Center → Password and security → Two-factor authentication → pick account → authentication app (recommended), SMS, or security key.

Accounts Center → Password and security → Where you're logged in.

Accounts Center → Password and security → Login alerts.

spec: in the app: Settings → Account → Two-step verification
verified: Path correct, but as of Aug 2026 the two-step verification PIN is now a full password (letters, numbers, symbols) - copy must not say 'six-digit PIN'. Also add passkey: Settings → Account → Passkeys (multiple passkeys allowed). WhatsApp has no security checkup; skip checkup.
Settings → Account → Two-step verification → Turn on (create password, add recovery email). Plus Settings → Account → Passkeys → Create passkey.
Recovery email inside Settings → Account → Two-step verification → Email address. Account is tied to the phone number, so keep the carrier PIN on (§6.3).
Settings → Linked Devices → tap device → Log Out.
No account password at login; the two-step password should be unique and saved in the Passwords app. Step applies to the two-step password.
Apply: 2fa, unique_pw (two-step password), recovery_info, sessions (Linked Devices). Skip: third_party, alerts, checkup.
https://x.com/settings/security_and_account_access (official; resolves to login). X has no checkup wizard; this is the Security and account access page.

Settings and privacy → Security and account access → Security → Two-factor authentication (authentication app or security key; SMS is X Premium only). Passkey: same Security screen → Additional password protection → Passkey.
Settings and privacy → Your account → Account information → Phone / Email.
Security and account access → Apps and sessions → Sessions (https://x.com/settings/sessions).
Security and account access → Apps and sessions → Connected apps (https://x.com/settings/connected_apps).
No login-alert toggle; X emails on new logins automatically. Informational.
Apply: 2fa, unique_pw, recovery_info, sessions, third_party, checkup (security page). Skip: alerts.
